claims.text: Laplace-LoRA reduces Expected Calibration Error (ECE) on LLaMA2-7B fine-tuned on Winogrande-small at 5000 gradient steps from 31.2% to 2.1%.
Laplace-LoRA reduces Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) on LLaMA2-7B fine-tuned on Winogrande-small at 5000 gradient steps from 3.15 to 0.60.
Laplace-LoRA incurs an additional memory overhead of 1% to 5% relative to standard LoRA fine-tuning.
Diagonal Fisher approximations in Laplace-LoRA fail to provide consistent calibration improvements compared to Kronecker-factored approximations.
Most of the logit uncertainty in full Laplace-LoRA originates from lower-layer LoRA parameters rather than the output layer.
Laplace-LoRA performs post-hoc Bayesian inference over LoRA parameters without modifying the underlying fine-tuned weight values.

evidence.description: Table 1 shows MAP fine-tuning achieves an ECE of 31.2% on Winogrande-small, whereas full Laplace-LoRA (LA) achieves an ECE of 2.1%.
Table 1 shows MAP fine-tuning achieves an NLL of 3.15 on Winogrande-small, whereas full Laplace-LoRA (LA) achieves an NLL of 0.60.
Table 4 and Section 5.3 demonstrate that implementing Laplace-LoRA adds only around 1-5% memory overhead over standard LoRA.
Section 5.2 and Appendix G.6 report that diagonal Laplace approximations do not offer consistent improvements in ECE and NLL.
Figure 12 and Appendix H analysis indicate that for full Laplace-LoRA, almost all logit variance stems from lower-layer parameters rather than the output layer.
Section 2 notes that Laplace-LoRA does not change fine-tuned weights and uses a Laplace approximation post-hoc to estimate uncertainty around weight MAP estimates.

methodologies.name: Laplace-LoRA
methodologies.description: Post-hoc Bayesian framework applying Kronecker-factored Laplace approximations over low-rank adaptation (LoRA) parameters in fine-tuned large language models.

limitations.text: Full-rank representation of the large Kronecker factor for LoRA layers is memory prohibitive, requiring a low-rank approximation.
Standard post-hoc calibration methods like temperature scaling rely on a separate validation set, which is problematic when data is scarce.
Applying Laplace approximation exclusively to the output layer (LLLA) provides inconsistent calibration performance across benchmark tasks.
